newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk parliament approves July 12 confidence vote.
newsitem.headline: Turk parliament approves July 12 confidence vote.

text.p: Turkey's parliament on Tuesday approved a decision to hold a vote of confidence on July 12 in the new anti-Islamist government of Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz.
Deputy speaker Hasan Korkmazcan announced the decision after deputies voted by a show of hands in favour of a recommendation made earlier on Tuesday by a parliamentary committee.
President Suleyman Demirel appointed conservative Yilmaz prime minister on Monday in a bid to keep the Islamists out of power after months of political chaos.

Yilmaz's chances of winning a confidence vote have been boosted by a wave of defections from a conservative faction allied to the Islam-based Welfare Party of outgoing Islamist prime minister Necmettin Erbakan.
The new left-right government, a minority coalition supported by a left-wing party, has around 12 more MPs on paper than its opponents in the 550-member national assembly.
The government's programme is to be read out in parliament on July 7 and then debated on July 10 ahead of the vote.
